Subject: Compliance add-ons — HSM licensing model question

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement here — a quick clarifying question before we loop legal: we need to understand the licensing options for HSM/KMS and residency.

Specifically GridHealth is evaluating two approaches for HSM:
- Per-seat (dedicated HSM seats billed monthly)
- Slab/commit model (N HSM seats purchased as a slab with a blended per-seat price, used across workloads)

Which model does Redwood prefer/recommend for a fast-scaling customer? For budgeting we also need to understand how residency tiers affect pricing (US-only vs multi-region) and whether audit log retention beyond 13 months is an extra line item.

Can you send a short one-pager or a pricing note we can attach to our PO? We need to get a PO to finance next week.

Subject: Re: Compliance add-ons — HSM licensing model question

Elena — thanks for the clear note and for coming to the demo. Short answer: both models are supported; tradeoffs below and recommendation. See attached worksheet for numbers.

Per-seat:
- Predictable mapping: each HSM seat is tied to a collector/instance; invoiced monthly.
- Easier for small, stable fleets.

Slab (commit):
- Buy a slab of N seats/slots for a period (annual or multi-year). Seats are pooled across projects; you can burst above slab at an overage rate or add additional slabs.
- Better unit economics for fast-scaling customers; we can offer stepped discounts at 3- and 6-slab points.

Residency tiers:
- US-only residency (data and keys in a US region with contractual data residency terms): +7% on the base compliance bundle by default (covers region-specific KMS/HSM footprint and operational separation).
- Multi-region (US + EU): additional +4% for cross-region replication and geo-redundant HSM keys.

Audit log retention: baseline 13 months included; extended retention (24/36 months) billed as a monthly TB increment.

Recommendation: For GridHealth’s growth profile Aaron described in the call, slab/commit gives the best price predictability and administrative simplicity. Id like to propose an initial 1-slab (12-seat equivalent) annual commitment with a 15% slab discount and an option to scale at pre-agreed tiers. If youd prefer per-seat we can present both line items.

Ive ccd Ben (pricing) and Marissa (contracts) to confirm concession runway and DOC routing. Attached: redwood-pricing-workback.xlsx with a quick workback and two scenarios (per-seat vs slab).

Best,

Markus — quick ops note on concessions and approval path:

Proposed commercial structure (recommended):
- 1-slab (12 seat-eq) annual commit
- List price per seat: $1,200/mo => slab effective $1,020/mo (15% slab discount)
- US-only residency uplift: +7% on the compliance bundle (applies to the slab net)
- Audit log ext retention (24 months): $40/TB/mo billed monthly

Approval gates:
- Up to 12% discount on list: Sales (Ben) signoff OK.
- 13–20%: require Sales director (Marissa) approval and finance review.

If Markus wants to push to 15% were already at it for the annual slab; anything above 15% will need Marissa to approve and well require a signed SOW or a minimum ARR commit. For GridHealth I recommend we hold the 15% as the public ask and confirm Marissa for any additional concession.

Ive updated the workbook with the discount waterfall and a projected monthly invoice example (tab: GridHealth_workback).

Ben
